To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lytic enzymes AlpA and AlbB of Lysobacter XL1 can be produced in the Pseudomonas Q2-87 strain, which is a good producer of recombinant proteins.
we have developed a novel expression system for (secreted) bacterial lytics, which allows for their production in a simple way and without cell lysis.
the lytic pepticases from Lysobacteria were expressed and secreted by Pseudomonas strains and the obtained proteins can be purified from the culture liquid by simple methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient system for the expression of lytic endopeptidases in the model bacterium P. fluorescens Q287.
the development of a system of expression of lytic enzymes of the Lysobacter group in the Pseudomonas genus.
the creation of a new system for the production of recombinant bacterial peptidases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the system of the expression and secretion of the AlpA and B lytic proteins in P. fluorescens Q287 is a good example of a successful application of a heterologous expression system for the production of lytic proteins.
the expression system developed in this work is a promising tool for the production of recombinant bacterial lytic enzymes in Pseudomonadaceae.
the presented data are the first report describing the expression of lytic endopeptidases from Lysobacteria in Pseudomonad cells.

we have developed an efficient expression system of lytic enzymes from Lysobactor sp. XL1, which are able to lyse gram-negative bacteria.
